title: The Missing Royal Letter
synopsis: A royal letter in the new letters is gone.
A false page is in its place.
goal: Find out who swapped the royal letter, and where the real one is.

notes: The gate book read as then, later and after: Mun-su goes home, Sora comes for the cups, Bae comes back last. Sunset and dawn are fixed; lunch is not part of the night.

learning.objective: 출입 장부의 순서 표현(then, later, after)을 읽고 밤에 일어난 일을 시간순으로 놓는다.
expressions: After Sora left, Copyist Bae came back for his brush.

play.title: The Gate Book
story: Autumn, 1446. The book of the new letters is finished.
The Royal Secretariat carries the King's orders.
Last night, a royal letter in the new letters waited in a box here.
At sunrise, Clerk Mun-su must deliver it to the palace scholars.
But at dawn, the letter is gone. A strange page is in the box.
play.letter:
At sunset, Mun-su locked the letter box.
Then he went home.
Later, Sora came in for the tea cups.
After Sora left, Copyist Bae came back for his brush.
Nobody came in after Bae.
At dawn, Mun-su opened the box.
play.question: Put the night in order. Who came in after the box was locked?
hints: Read the gate book. Look for then, later and after.
Mun-su ate lunch in the day, not at night. Set that card aside.
play.successMessage: Two people came in after the box was locked!
transition: Two people came in after sunset: Sora and Bae.
"Bae is the palace copyist," says Taek. "He draws a little leaf on every page he copies."
Mun-su shows you the strange page.
play.orderFeedback: Read the gate book again. Who came in after Sora?

clue.title: After Sunset
clue.note: After Mun-su locked the box, Sora came in, then Bae. Nobody came in after Bae.

TEMPORARY PICTURE (pilot only, never the Seoul season's): both papers are Paris Case 03's blank work log (measured): a clipboard, not a Joseon paper.

learning.objective: 두 문서의 같은 줄을 비교해 내용이 다른 줄(WHY)을 찾는다.

play.title: Two Papers
story: The strange page looks like the royal letter.
Mun-su also has the scholars' sheet about the new letters.
"The page should be a copy of the King's words," he whispers.
play.letter:
There are 28 letters.
Five main consonant letters copy the shapes we make to speak.
They show the tongue, the mouth, the teeth and the throat.
The dot is the round sky. The flat line is the flat earth. The standing line is a person.
The King made them so people can learn them easily and use them every day.
The book says a slow person can learn them in ten days.
Now find the line on the page that does not match.
play.question: Which line does not match?
hints: Read the WHY line on each paper.
One says EASY TO LEARN. What does the other say?
transition: The strange page is written in the new letters.
At the bottom of it, someone drew a small leaf.
You go to the copy room.

clue.title: The Changed Line
clue.note: The page says SCHOLARS ONLY. The King's words say EASY TO LEARN.

play.title: Ink in the Copy Room
story: Sora and Bae came in after sunset.
Sora had a paper in her sleeve.
Bae says he only took his brush.
play.letterIntro: Your notes on the marks in the copy room:
play.letter:
Drops of fresh black ink lead across the rug.
A long brush hair is caught under a lid.
A torn corner of thick paper sticks out of the same box.
play.question: Where is the royal letter hidden?
hints: Tap the ink, the brush hair and the paper corner.
Which box has a lid and stands on the rug?
play.successMessage: The royal letter is in the small chest!
transition: It is Bae's chest. Inside, the letter is wrapped in a brush cloth. The name BAE is sewn on it.
Sora is pale. She shows you the paper from her sleeve.
"It is my practice page," she says. "I learned the new letters in ten days."
She is not the thief. Her page shows a dot, a flat line and a standing line, again and again.

play.title: The Copyist Answers
story: Bae waits in the palace yard.
Bae claims he did nothing wrong.
play.letter:
Bae came in last, after sunset.
The false page has a small leaf at the bottom.
The letter was wrapped in Bae's brush cloth.
play.question: Answer each claim with one piece of evidence.
hints: Bae makes three claims. Answer each one with one piece of evidence.
Use the gate book, the false page and the wrapped letter.
transition: "If everyone can write, who will pay me to write for them?" he asks.
Mun-su hands him the scholars' sheet. "Then teach them. You learned the new letters too."
The sun is up. Before Mun-su delivers the royal letter, Sora reads its first line with him.

evidence.name: Bae's Story
evidence.description: Bae swapped the letter. He was afraid of losing his work.

interview.speaker: bae
interview.goal: Show that Bae swapped the royal letter.

opening.text: I am only a copyist. I did nothing.
Then let us look at my notebook.

lines.text: I write letters for people who cannot write. They pay me.

presents.prompt: Bae says: "I went home before sunset."

lines.text: The gate book… Yes. I came back for my brush.

presents.miss: That does not show when I came in.
presents.tell: The gate book shows who came in after sunset.

presents.prompt: Bae says: "I cannot even write the new letters!"

lines.text: This page is in the new letters. It has your little leaf.
I draw that leaf on every copy. I wrote it.

presents.tell: The false page is in the new letters, with a small leaf.

presents.prompt: Bae says: "Anyone could put a letter in my chest!"

lines.text: The letter was wrapped in your brush cloth. Your name is sewn on it.

presents.miss: That does not show who hid the letter.
presents.tell: The letter was wrapped in Bae's own brush cloth.

play.orderFeedback: Show one piece of evidence for each claim.

hook: The royal letter must be delivered at sunrise.

intro: Autumn, 1446. A royal letter is gone.

It must be delivered at sunrise.
